description:
Get organization-wide activity summaries for a date range.

Returns one entry per day from `starting_date` (inclusive) to `ending_date`
(exclusive) in `data`, the same `data` / `next_page` envelope as the other
analytics list endpoints; the series is currently returned in full, so
`next_page` is always null.
Data is typically available with a 1-day lag and may be revised by a few
percent over the following days: when `ending_date` is omitted it
defaults to the most recent available day + 1, so the last entry covers
the most recent available day. The series can be scoped to an RBAC group
via `filter[]=rbac_group_id:{id}`. Available to organizations on a Claude
Enterprise plan. Requires an API key with the `read:analytics` scope.

parameters.description: UTC date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Start of the date range (inclusive). Data is typically available with a 1-day lag (varies by query; the error for a too-recent date names the latest available day) and may be revised by a few percent over the following days. No earlier than 2026-01-01.
parameters.name: starting_date

schema.description: UTC date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Start of the date range (inclusive). Data is typically available with a 1-day lag (varies by query; the error for a too-recent date names the latest available day) and may be revised by a few percent over the following days. No earlier than 2026-01-01.
schema.title: Starting Date

parameters.description: UTC date in YYYY-MM-DD format. End of the date range (exclusive). Data is typically available with a 1-day lag, so this can be at most today — which is also the default when omitted, making the last entry cover the most recent available day. Data may be revised by a few percent over the following days. The range may span at most 366 days.
parameters.name: ending_date

schema.description: UTC date in YYYY-MM-DD format. End of the date range (exclusive). Data is typically available with a 1-day lag, so this can be at most today — which is also the default when omitted, making the last entry cover the most recent available day. Data may be revised by a few percent over the following days. The range may span at most 366 days.
schema.title: Ending Date

parameters.description: Number of results per page (1-1000, default 100). The day series (at most 366 entries) is currently returned in full in a single page, so `limit` does not yet shorten it.
parameters.name: limit

schema.description: Number of results per page (1-1000, default 100). The day series (at most 366 entries) is currently returned in full in a single page, so `limit` does not yet shorten it.
schema.title: Limit

parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response's `next_page` field. `next_page` is currently always null, so there is never a cursor to send.
parameters.name: page

schema.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response's `next_page` field. `next_page` is currently always null, so there is never a cursor to send.
schema.title: Page

parameters.description: Filters as `dimension:value`. Only `rbac_group_id` is supported (e.g. `filter[]=rbac_group_id:{id}`); repeat the param to OR across groups. Scopes the whole day series to members of the matching group(s), re-aggregated from member-level activity — org-wide seat/invite fields and the adoption rates derived from them are null on scoped rows. `rbac_group_id` accepts the tagged id (`rbac_group_...`, as emitted in responses and by the spend-limits API) or a bare group UUID, and matches users who held the group at any point during each UTC day (time-of-usage attribution). At most 100 entries.
parameters.name: filter[]

At most 100 entries.

data.description: One entry per day in the requested range, ascending by date.
